values: As a returning player, I want to resume my saved campaign, So that I can continue without reselecting setup options.
When activeCampaignState exists, the setup screen shows a resume card and restores the selected country, scenario, language, diplomatic partner, and active state.
Review setup/resume code; run macOS XCTest suite; verify launch succeeds.
Resume path is implemented and covered by persistence tests for active campaign restoration.
Passed in full macOS XCTest run.
As a strategy player, I want to choose a scenario before starting, So that the campaign begins in the intended historical timeline.
Scenario cards show the catalog, selecting one updates selectedScenarioID, and country names/starting state reflect the selected scenario.
Review scenario picker and scenario catalog; run macOS XCTest suite.
Scenario selection is implemented and backed by scenario expansion/customization tests.
Passed in full macOS XCTest run.
As a player, I want to choose the app language, So that game content and UI use my preferred language.
Language picker updates store.selectedLanguage, app language preferences, and game state language; settings explains that restart may be required for full interface refresh.
Review setup/settings language flows; run lint and macOS XCTest suite.
Language selection exists in setup and settings, persists through store APIs, and localized string resources are present.
Passed in lint and full macOS XCTest run.
AI provider setup before campaign start
As a player using AI turns, I want to select and configure the AI provider before starting, So that the first campaign turn can use the provider I chose.

Setup exposes Apple Foundation Models, OpenRouter Free Router, and Z.AI choices; external providers require API keys before continuing; countries cannot be started until the selected provider is usable.

Apple/PaxHistoriaApple/CountrySelectionView.swift providerSetupDeck providerCard apiKeyField; Apple/PaxHistoriaApple/NativeCampaignStore.swift provider setters; selectors native-provider-* native-provider-continue native-provider-start-warning
Review macOS and iOS setup flow; patch missing macOS setup; run lint, full macOS XCTest, and build_and_run verification.
Provider setup is now present in macOS setup and country rows are disabled until provider requirements are met.
Mac setup previously skipped provider setup and could enter campaign with an unusable external provider.
Added providerSetupDeck to macOS setup, provider warning row, and country start gating.
Passed lint, full macOS XCTest, and build_and_run verification.
As a player starting a campaign, I want to search for a country, So that I can quickly find the country I want to play.
Search filters by country name or code, clear resets the query, and an empty state appears when there are no matches.
Apple/PaxHistoriaApple/CountrySelectionView.swift searchField countryList clearSearch; selectors native-country-search native-country-empty native-clear-country-search
Review search/filter code and iOS UI path; update iOS UI test for provider setup; run lint, macOS XCTest suite, and iOS UI smoke test.
Search, clear, and empty-state UI are implemented; iOS UI test now reaches search after provider selection.
iOS UI test flow was stale because provider setup now appears before country search.
Updated PaxHistoriaiOSUITests to select provider and continue before searching.
Passed lint, full macOS XCTest, and dedicated iOS Simulator UI smoke test.
As a new player, I want to start as a selected country, So that a playable campaign state is created.
Choosing a country initializes state for the selected scenario/language/provider, persists the selected country, and requests suggestions when appropriate.
Apple/PaxHistoriaApple/CountrySelectionView.swift CountryCard choose; Apple/PaxHistoriaApple/NativeCampaignStore.swift choose; selectors native-country-option-* native-country-continue
Review choose flow and provider gating; run full macOS XCTest and launch verification.
Campaign start path creates state; start buttons now respect provider readiness.
Start controls could be reached while provider configuration was incomplete.
Disabled country start until the provider deck reports usable configuration.
Passed full macOS XCTest and build_and_run verification.
As a desktop player, I want a sidebar and toolbar for campaign sections, So that I can move quickly between map, orders, intelligence, economy, library, and settings.

The macOS shell uses split navigation with Overview, Orders, Intelligence, Economics, Library, and Settings destinations, plus an optional inspector and toolbar shortcuts for advance and advisor actions.

Apple/PaxHistoriaApple/NativeGameShell.swift NativeGameShell; Apple/PaxHistoriaApple/NativeGameShellShared.swift NativeMacDestination; selectors native-mac-split-shell native-mac-inspector-toggle native-mac-toolbar-advance
Review split-view destinations, toolbar and inspector bindings; run full macOS XCTest and launch verification.
macOS navigation destinations and toolbar shortcuts are implemented and app launches successfully.
As a mobile player, I want tabs and compact command buttons, So that I can access core game actions on a small screen.
The iOS shell exposes Map, Orders, and Intel tabs plus command buttons/drawer for orders, advisor, diplomacy, and advance.
Apple/PaxHistoriaApple/NativeGameView.swift TabView NativeMapCommandBar CommandConsoleDrawer; selectors native-tab-map native-tab-orders native-tab-intel native-command-*
Review iOS tabs and command drawer; run all 29 PaxHistoriaiOSUITests on the iOS 26.5 simulator.
Map, Orders and Intel tabs, the compact command bar, command console drawer and all intelligence sections are implemented and exercised by the iOS UI suite.
Passed the full 29-test iOS Simulator UI suite.
As a first-time player, I want guided contextual help, So that I understand campaign controls before playing.
On first campaign entry, contextual help pages can be advanced, skipped, or completed; reduced-motion preferences are respected by related visual effects.
Review contextual help state and controls; run macOS XCTest suite.
Help overlay state and controls are implemented with persistent completion behavior.
As a campaign player, I want an overview dashboard, So that I can understand national status, objectives, recent orders, and next decisions.
Overview renders hero status, metrics, objectives, recent orders, advisor prompts, and map/intelligence summaries with responsive macOS/mobile composition.
Apple/PaxHistoriaApple/NativeOverviewComponents.swift NativeOverviewScreen NativeMetricsGrid NativeCampaignObjectivesPanel NativeAfterActionReportPanel; selector native-overview-header
Review overview screen composition; run build_and_run verification.
Overview dashboard is implemented and reachable from app shell.
As a strategist, I want map layers and a legend, So that I can inspect relations, conflict, economy, and fallout at a glance.
Map supports layer selection, legend rendering, relation/conflict/economic/fallout overlays, and region selection.
Review map components and layer model; run lint and build verification.
Layer picker, map, and legend code are implemented and compile.
As a strategist, I want to zoom and inspect regions, So that I can focus on local conditions and choose regional actions.
Map controls adjust zoom/position, selecting a region opens a dossier, and regional actions are disabled when command capacity is insufficient.
Apple/PaxHistoriaApple/NativeMapComponents.swift RegionDetailsCard regional actions; Apple/PaxHistoriaApple/NativeWorldMap.swift; selectors native-region-dossier native-regional-action-*
Review zoom, selection, and dossier code; run lint.
Region dossier and regional action disable states are implemented.
As a player, I want to advance time by selected intervals, So that planned actions resolve through the AI engine.
Advance controls offer 1, 3, and 12 month jumps, show progress, call selected provider, validate the generated turn, apply results, and surface provider/validation errors.
Apple/PaxHistoriaApple/NativeGameView.swift NativeAdvanceMenu NativeFloatingAdvanceButton; Apple/PaxHistoriaApple/NativeCampaignStore.swift advance performAdvance; selectors native-advance-*
Review advance menu/store flow; run full macOS XCTest and build verification.
Advance flow is implemented and tested across provider routing and validation paths.
Passed full macOS XCTest and build_and_run verification.
As a player waiting for AI resolution, I want visible turn progress, So that I know the app is working and which provider/model is active.
During turn generation the overlay shows phase, progress, provider/model summary, and console-style logs; reduce-motion settings avoid decorative animation.

Apple/PaxHistoriaApple/NativeGameShellShared.swift NativeTurnProgressPanel; Apple/PaxHistoriaApple/NativeCampaignStore.swift turnProgress; selectors native-turn-progress-panel native-turn-progress-bar native-turn-provider-summary native-turn-model-identifier
Review overlay and store progress updates; run lint/build verification.
Progress overlay is implemented and compiles.
As a player after a time jump, I want a turn report, So that I can review what changed before continuing.
After a successful turn, a report sheet shows summary, metrics, events, and action results; closing clears the report state.

Apple/PaxHistoriaApple/NativeGameView.swift report sheet binding; Apple/PaxHistoriaApple/NativeGameView+Report.swift NativeTurnReportView; selectors native-turn-report native-report-close native-report-dismiss
Review report sheet and close handling; run macOS XCTest suite.
Turn report sheet is implemented and report state is cleared through store flow.
As a player who reaches an end state, I want a clear victory or defeat message, So that I understand the campaign outcome and can exit cleanly.
When victoryStatus is no longer ongoing, a blocking overlay explains the outcome and offers exit to main menu.
Review victory status handling and overlay; run macOS XCTest suite.
Victory/defeat overlay and exit path are implemented.
As a player, I want to write my own order, So that I can plan custom strategic actions.
The order editor accepts title/details, previews cost/effects, disables add for empty or over-capacity orders, and inserts valid orders into the queue.
Review editor validation and store insertion; run macOS XCTest suite.
Manual order creation and validation paths are implemented.
As a player drafting an order, I want a preview of cost and likely effects, So that I can avoid invalid or wasteful actions.
Preview shows command cost, remaining capacity, projected effects, and warnings before the order is added.
Review preview panel and engine preview code; run lint.
Directive preview exists and warning logic compiles.
As a player, I want quick action templates, So that I can add common orders without writing from scratch.
Templates are grouped by category and create planned orders with localized titles/details and command costs.
Review quick action catalog and picker; run full macOS XCTest.
Quick action templates are implemented and accepted by store insertion paths.
As a player managing the queue, I want to remove planned orders, So that I can recover command capacity before advancing.
Deleting an order removes it from plannedActions and refunds command capacity up to the maximum cap.
Review delete/refund store logic; run macOS XCTest suite.
Delete/refund behavior is implemented and covered by backend tests.
As a player, I want AI-suggested orders, So that I can turn advisor recommendations into queued actions quickly.
Suggested actions can be refreshed from the selected provider, show loading/error/empty states, and accepting a suggestion adds it as a planned action.

Apple/PaxHistoriaApple/NativeOrdersComponents.swift NativeSuggestedActionsPanel; Apple/PaxHistoriaApple/NativeCampaignStore.swift refreshSuggestedActions addSuggestedAction; selectors native-refresh-suggestions native-use-suggestion-*
Review suggestions panel/provider/store path; run macOS XCTest suite.
Suggestion refresh, error, empty, and accept paths are implemented.
As a player, I want to ask the advisor a question, So that I can get contextual strategic guidance.
Advisor question input disables empty/loading submissions, sends the prompt to the selected provider, persists transcript entries, and shows provider errors without losing the question.
Review advisor UI and store error handling; run macOS XCTest suite.
Advisor ask flow and provider error preservation are implemented.
As a player, I want to message another country, So that I can negotiate or probe diplomatic positions.
The diplomacy panel selects a partner, sends a message through the selected provider, appends the reply to the thread, and shows provider errors without fabricating a reply.

Apple/PaxHistoriaApple/NativeIntelComponents.swift NativeDiplomacyPanel; Apple/PaxHistoriaApple/NativeCampaignStore.swift sendDiplomaticMessage; selectors native-diplomacy-partner native-diplomacy-message native-send-diplomacy
Review diplomacy panel and store flow; run macOS XCTest suite.
Diplomatic messaging and error handling are implemented.
As a player receiving offers, I want to accept, counter, or reject proposals, So that treaty outcomes affect the campaign state.
Pending offers show accept/counter/reject actions; accepting/countering updates offer status, relationships, ledger, and timeline; accepted offers appear in the treaty stack.
Review offer controls and store methods; run macOS XCTest suite.
Offer controls, status changes, ledger entries, and treaty stack are implemented.
As a strategist, I want to inspect the diplomatic network, So that I can understand major actors and relationships.
Network panel summarizes top actors, relationship scores, agendas, and diplomatic posture for the current campaign.
Review network panel code; run lint/build verification.
Diplomatic network panel is implemented and reachable in intelligence surfaces.
As a player, I want to read campaign events, So that I can understand recent world changes and action consequences.
Events screen lists timeline events with kind, importance, description, and empty-state messaging when no events exist.
Review events panel code; run build verification.
Events timeline and empty state are implemented.
As a player, I want economic panels and budget sliders, So that I can track finances and set national priorities.
Economics panels show player budget, world economic cards, fog-of-war masking, and budget sliders that rebalance to a 100 percent allocation.
Review economics panels and budget update logic; run macOS XCTest suite.
Economic panels and budget balancing logic are implemented.
As a player, I want to adjust difficulty and scenario settings, So that I can tailor the campaign mode and restart scenario-specific state when needed.
Settings expose difficulty/game mode and scenario selection; scenario changes reinitialize campaign state according to selected scenario rules.
Review settings controls and store mutations; run macOS XCTest suite.
Difficulty/scenario settings are implemented and covered by scenario/state tests.
AI provider status and API keys
As a player configuring AI, I want provider status and key fields, So that I know whether the selected AI path can run turns.
Settings expose provider picker, OpenRouter/Z.AI key fields, status checks, and warning copy that matches the selected provider without implying silent fallback.
Review provider settings/status copy; patch stale copy; run lint and full macOS XCTest.
Provider settings are implemented and copy now accurately says OpenRouter requires an API key.
OpenRouter text previously suggested fallback behavior inconsistent with selected-provider correctness.
Updated OpenRouter subtitle/warning copy to describe required API key without implying fallback.
Passed lint and full macOS XCTest run.
As a player, I want visible save slots, So that I can switch between campaigns without hidden state management.
Settings show three save slots with active/empty summaries; switching slots immediately loads that slot or returns to setup when empty.

Apple/PaxHistoriaApple/NativeSettingsComponents.swift NativeSaveSlotPicker; Apple/PaxHistoriaApple/NativeCampaignStore+Persistence.swift switchSlot slotSummary; selectors native-save-slot-picker native-save-slot-summary-*
Review persistence APIs and settings surface; add missing UI; run lint, full macOS XCTest, and build verification.
Save slot UI is now present in settings and uses existing slot APIs.
Save-slot backend existed but had no visible settings control for players.
Added NativeSaveSlotPicker and inserted it into settings after the scenario picker.
Passed lint, full macOS XCTest, and build_and_run verification.
As a player, I want to import and export campaign data, So that I can back up or move a campaign.
Library exports campaign JSON with a generated filename, imports validated JSON, rejects oversize/invalid data, and shows success/error messages.

Apple/PaxHistoriaApple/NativeIntelComponents.swift NativeLibraryPanel; Apple/PaxHistoriaApple/NativeGameView.swift fileImporter fileExporter; Apple/PaxHistoriaApple/NativeCampaignStore.swift exportCampaignData importCampaignData; selectors native-export-campaign native-import-campaign native-library-message
Review library panel, importer/exporter, and store validation; run macOS XCTest suite.
Import/export flows and validation are implemented.
As a player, I want local saves to recover from interruption or corruption, So that campaign progress is not lost unnecessarily.

Persistence writes slot-scoped envelopes, backups and legacy copies; prefers the newest valid save; falls back to backup/legacy data; debounces rapid noncritical mutations; and writes critical new-game, import, manual-save and turn mutations immediately.
Review persistence precedence and debounce paths; run save-slot, recovery, import/export and full macOS tests.
Slot-scoped persistence, backup fallback, legacy import, coalesced background writes and immediate critical writes are implemented and tested.
As a player selecting an AI provider, I want all AI surfaces to use that provider, So that turns, suggestions, advisor, and diplomacy stay consistent.
DynamicAIService routes turn generation, suggestions, advisor, diplomacy and remote world-simulation prompts through the selected provider; OpenRouter free mode does not silently fall back to Apple.
Run provider-routing, response-repair, world-simulator parsing and full macOS tests; inspect visible provider identity and missing-key errors.
Provider routing tests now pass and validate all game AI surfaces through OpenRouter free mode.
Test fixture generated an invalid linkedActionID when no planned action existed, causing provider-routing test failure.
Updated CapturingOpenRouterGameService fixture to emit null linkedActionID when there is no planned action.
Focused routing test and full macOS XCTest passed.
As a player encountering failures, I want clear visible errors, So that I know what failed and what I can fix.
Provider errors, import errors, suggestion failures, recovery warnings, and validation failures are shown through banners/warnings instead of silent failure.
Review error-state UI and store error assignments; run macOS XCTest suite.
Error banners/warnings are implemented across provider, import, suggestion, and persistence paths.
As a player changing state during AI work, I want stale responses ignored, So that old provider replies cannot corrupt the current campaign.
State versioning and cancellation invalidate in-flight turn/suggestion/advisor/diplomacy work after reset, import, slot switch, or campaign replacement.
Apple/PaxHistoriaApple/NativeCampaignStore.swift stateVersion cancelInFlightTurn invalidateInFlightWork; provider task call sites
Review async guard implementation and tests; run macOS XCTest suite.
Stale-response guards and cancellation hooks are implemented and covered by backend/error-path tests.
As a keyboard, VoiceOver, or automation user, I want controls to have labels and stable identifiers, So that the app is navigable and testable.
Core setup, navigation, orders, advisor, diplomacy, map, import/export, provider, and save-slot controls expose accessibility labels/identifiers; motion-heavy surfaces respect reduce-motion state.
Inventory explicit stable and dynamic identifiers; run lint, macOS tests and all iOS UI tests; inspect reduce-motion branches and child-element containment.

Core setup, navigation, map, orders, intelligence, settings, import/export and save controls expose labels/identifiers; motion-heavy surfaces check reduced-motion state. Testing found and fixed hidden child controls in the order row and country-search field. A human VoiceOver traversal remains an external manual limitation.
Missing identifiers would have made new provider/save-slot UI harder to test if left unaddressed.
Added identifiers for provider start warning and save-slot picker/summary rows.
Passed lint, macOS tests and all iOS UI tests; code-level accessibility audit passed.
Native offline behavior and no service worker
As a native app user, I want offline expectations to be clear, So that local saves work while provider-backed AI actions fail visibly without network/API access.
The active Apple app has no service worker; offline resilience is local persistence/import/export plus visible provider errors when external AI cannot be reached.
Apple/PaxHistoriaApple/README.md; Apple/PaxHistoriaApple/NativeCampaignStore+Persistence.swift; Apple/PaxHistoriaApple/NativeOpenRouterService.swift; no service-worker files in active Apple surface
Inspect active Apple surface for service-worker/PWA code; review persistence and provider error paths.
No service worker is implemented in the active native product; local persistence and provider error paths cover offline behavior.
No fix needed; documented as not applicable to native Apple app.
Reviewed current codebase and final report documents scope.
Manual save, reset, and exit to menu
As a player, I want save/reset/exit controls, So that I can preserve progress, clear a campaign, or return to setup intentionally.
Settings exposes manual save unless ironman mode makes autosave authoritative, reset clears the selected slot/campaign, and exit returns to setup while preserving restorable state.
Review settings action controls and persistence methods; run macOS XCTest suite.
Manual save, reset, and exit-to-menu flows are implemented with persistence hooks.
As a player using remote providers, I want rate-limit handling, So that the app behaves predictably under provider throttling or transient failures.
Remote provider calls use rate limiter/backoff paths, report provider-specific errors, and expose selected-provider status without leaking secrets.
Review rate limiter and provider services; run full macOS XCTest suite.
Rate limiter and provider error mapping are implemented; live provider tests skip without environment keys.
Passed full macOS XCTest; live provider tests skipped because no live API env was configured.
As a maintainer, I want iOS UI tests to follow the real player flows, So that setup, navigation, orders, intelligence, settings, library and turn-report regressions are caught.

The 29-test suite covers provider-first setup, scenario/back/search controls, campaign launch, tabs and console, order add/delete/suggestions, advisor, diplomacy, advance intervals/report dismissal, library buttons and settings actions.
Run script/lint.sh and all PaxHistoriaiOSUITests on the iOS 26.5 simulator.
The first complete run exposed order-row, intelligence/settings and setup regressions. All 29 iOS UI tests pass after app accessibility fixes and selector/scroll corrections.

Lint scanned generated Swift; the order-row container hid its delete child; intelligence tests used removed section IDs and did not scroll horizontal/vertical content; setup tests targeted obsolete Back labels; the search container hid its clear button.

Excluded Apple/PaxHistoriaApple/.build from SwiftLint; exposed child accessibility controls in order/search rows; assigned stable setup back/clear identifiers; scrolled to queued orders and off-screen settings/intelligence controls; replaced removed intelligence IDs with the six current sections.
script/lint.sh passes with zero violations; all 29 iOS UI tests pass.

As a player starting a campaign, I want my selected country (and AI countries) to have a defined government type (democracy, autocracy, hybrid), So that political rules and starting configurations are correctly initialized.
Country profile matches historical starting baseline (e.g., CHN is autocracy, RUS is hybrid, others default to democracy) during scenario initialization.
Verify database initializes CHN as autocracy, RUS as hybrid, and others as democracy; run political system unit tests.
Implemented in the current Apple-native code and covered by the current political-system backend tests.
Passed the full macOS XCTest suite in the current worktree.
Political Systems - Public Approval and Regime Support Tracking

As a player managing a country, I want to track my nation's public approval rating or regime support over time in the metrics grid and economic overview, So that I can monitor political stability and public satisfaction.
Overview dashboard shows Government and Public Approval/Regime Support cards, and the World Economics panel details show Government and Approval/Support rows for selected countries.

Open Overview screen and World Economics panel; verify that Government Type and Public Approval/Regime Support are displayed with correct labels (Public Approval for democracies, Regime Support for autocracies/hybrids).
Implemented in the current Apple-native code and covered by the current political-system backend tests.
Passed the full macOS XCTest suite in the current worktree.

As a player playing as a democracy or autocracy, I want relationships between nations of similar ideologies to improve over time and relationships between differing ideologies to decay over time, So that geopolitical blocs form naturally.

AI drift updates relationship scores between countries: nations with same government types drift positive (+0.05 per month), whereas democracy vs autocracy relationships drift negative (-0.1 per month).
Run AI drift drift logic over 12 months; assert democracy-democracy relationship rises and democracy-autocracy decays.
Implemented in the current Apple-native code and covered by the current political-system backend tests.
Passed the full macOS XCTest suite in the current worktree.

As a player running a democracy, I want periodic democratic elections to occur based on my country's next election round, So that my continuation in power depends on public approval, with low approval leading to opposition victories, policy/doctrine shifts (for AI), and stability hits.

When current round reaches nextElectionRound for a democracy, an election is resolved. Win chance is equal to public approval. Opposition victory resets approval to 55%, sets next election in 48 rounds, shifts AI doctrine and budget priority, and imposes a -5 stability hit on the player country.
Trigger advance turn past nextElectionRound; check for logged election events in timeline, next election round updates, and stability delta on opposition win.
Implemented in the current Apple-native code and covered by the current political-system backend tests.
Passed the full macOS XCTest suite in the current worktree.

As a player running an autocracy, I want critically low regime support to trigger potential coup attempts, So that unstable autocracies risk overthrow, causing severe stability drops, policy shifts, and decayed relations with democracies.

Autocracies with regime support below 25% have a 30% chance per month of a coup. A coup causes a -15 stability hit for players, resets support to 45%, shifts AI country doctrine to defensive/isolationist, resets budget to stability, and decays relations with democracies by -40.
Set autocracy approval to 15%; run simulateAIDrift multiple turns; check that coup fires, logs a timeline event, decays relations with democracies, and reduces player stability.
Implemented in the current Apple-native code and covered by the current political-system backend tests.
Passed the full macOS XCTest suite in the current worktree.
As a new player, I want a clear scenario-to-provider-to-country setup flow with back controls, So that I can revise earlier choices without restarting the app.

The setup advances from scenario selection to provider configuration to searchable country selection; Back returns one step while preserving valid choices; clear search restores the full country list.

Apple/PaxHistoriaApple/CountrySelectionView.swift setupStep scenarioDeck providerCard searchField; Apple/PaxHistoriaAppleUITests/PaxHistoriaiOSUITests.swift setup navigation tests; selectors native-provider-back native-country-back native-provider-continue native-country-search native-country-clear-search
Run scenario selection, provider-card, provider-back, country-back and clear-search iOS UI tests.

The first full UI run found both back-navigation tests targeting an obsolete generic label and found the clear-search child hidden by its parent accessibility label. Stable controls now expose the intended behavior.
Setup back controls lacked stable test identifiers, and the country-search container hid its clear-search child from the accessibility tree.
Added stable identifiers for both back controls and the clear button; changed the search row to contain its child elements; updated tests to assert the cleared field value.
Focused setup tests and the final full 29-test iOS UI suite pass.
As a player who wants remote backup, I want to configure a Turso save mirror, So that local-first campaign saves can also be copied to my database.

Settings accepts a libsql/https database URL and token; when both are configured, local saves remain authoritative and an authenticated background upsert mirrors primary, backup and legacy blobs without exposing the token.

Apple/PaxHistoriaApple/NativeSettingsComponents.swift TURSO SAVE MIRROR fields; Apple/PaxHistoriaApple/NativeCampaignStore+Persistence.swift writeTursoPersistenceData; Apple/PaxHistoriaApple/NativeCampaignStore.swift TursoConfiguration TursoWritePipeline; selectors native-turso-database-url native-turso-auth-token
Review settings fields and local-first copy; run Turso URL normalization, request construction, auth-header and response-decoding tests.
Optional Turso configuration and background write pipeline are implemented; local persistence remains usable when Turso is absent or unavailable.
Passed Turso configuration/pipeline tests and full macOS XCTest.
As a player resolving nonregional orders, I want success, partial-success or failure outcomes with visible consequences, So that orders carry risk instead of always succeeding.

Resolved nonregional actions roll deterministically from action ID and round, adjust chance by stability, record outcome on the order, create timeline consequences, apply failure penalties and show outcome badges in order/report rows.
Run deterministic success/failure tests; inspect outcome badge rendering and timeline/ledger mutations; run full macOS XCTest.
Success and failure paths resolve deterministically, persist outcome state and expose visible report/timeline feedback.
Passed action-outcome tests and full macOS XCTest.
As a head of government, I want political reform orders, So that I can call elections or deliberately change the constitutional regime with meaningful risk.

Political quick actions expose snap election, liberalization, executive consolidation, constitutional suspension and electoral reform; capacity costs and regime prerequisites apply; deterministic resolution updates government type, approval, election timing, stability, diplomacy and timeline feedback.
Review political action cards and costs; run liberalization success/failure, consolidation and snap-election backend tests; run full macOS XCTest.
All five reform templates are present and tested resolution paths update political ledgers and visible events.
Passed political-reform tests and full macOS XCTest.
As a military strategist, I want terrain, budgets, units and fortifications to affect combat, So that regional invasions and defense choices have legible tactical consequences.

Map regions receive deterministic terrain and show terrain modifiers; invasion previews mention risk; combat dice incorporate terrain, military budget, units and fortress level; background armies scale from GDP, military spending and corruption; results appear in timeline/report events.

Apple/PaxHistoriaApple/GeopoliticalMapData.swift determineTerrain; Apple/PaxHistoriaApple/NativeWorldMap.swift terrain rendering and RegionDetailsCard; Apple/PaxHistoriaApple/NativeGameEngine.swift invasion resolution; Apple/PaxHistoriaApple/BackgroundSimulationService.swift startingArmy
Inspect region dossier/terrain labels; run invasion, linked-invasion, 512-dice, regional-order, military-building and background-simulation tests.
Terrain is visible in the dossier/map and materially participates in deterministic player/AI combat resolution and force initialization.
Passed combat, regional-order, background-simulation and full macOS tests.
As a player advancing a remote-provider campaign, I want important AI countries to take bounded independent actions, So that the world evolves beyond direct reactions to my nation.

Every third completed turn for OpenRouter or Z.AI, up to three nonplayer countries are selected by salience; one unique bounded decision per selected country becomes a target-dated timeline/report event, applies to the correct target ledger/global track, records last action, and secondary-simulation failure does not discard the main turn.
Run world-simulator parsing/selection/date/clamp tests; run foreign-target effect isolation test; inspect performAdvance integration; run full macOS XCTest.

Initially, world-simulator events were inserted after engine application, so effects and turn reports omitted them; counters aged only on simulation turns; duplicate/unselected decisions were accepted; foreign stability effects could bleed into player stability. All paths now use bounded, target-aware engine application.
World-simulator decisions bypassed core application/reporting and target isolation, undermining the advertised measurable world effects.

Moved world simulation before engine application, target-dated and filtered unique allowed decisions, applied events through the main engine/report path, aged salience each turn, preserved deterministic doctrine updates and filtered player-only stability/report effects.
Focused world-simulator and foreign-target tests pass; full macOS XCTest passes.
As a player occupying another country, I want that country's allies to react diplomatically, So that territorial aggression has coherent relationship costs.

For each foreign region occupied by the player, AI countries with a relationship above 50 to the defender reduce their relationship with the player by a bounded monthly penalty before normal ideological drift.
Create a player occupation and an AI ally of the defender; simulate one month; verify the ally relationship with the player falls by the occupation penalty and remains clamped.

The source loop identified allies and read the current score but never wrote the penalty, so occupations produced no allied reaction. The relationship mutation is now applied and covered by a focused test.
Defender allies did not penalize the player after foreign occupation because the calculated relationship score was discarded.
Apply the bounded monthly relationship penalty back to each qualifying ally state and added deterministic coverage.
Focused allied-occupation test passes; full macOS XCTest passes.
